body.text: The Diplomat author Mercy Kuo regularly engages subject-matter experts, policy practitioners, and strategic thinkers across the globe for their diverse insights into U.S. Asia policy. This conversation with Maggie Wu – co-founder and CEO of VelaFi, a stablecoin-powered payments and treasury infrastructure company connecting businesses across Latin America, Asia, and the United States – is the 535th in “The Trans-Pacific View Insight Series.”
What was the impetus behind your decision to found VelaFi?

VelaFi grew out of the challenges I encountered while investing and building businesses in Latin America. Originally from China, I moved to the United States and spent much of my career in entrepreneurship and investment. In 2017, I co-founded blockchain investment firm Krypital Group. While exploring investment opportunities in Latin America in 2019, I saw businesses struggling with currency volatility, limited financial access, and expensive, slow cross-border payments. For companies trading with Asia, these challenges directly affected purchasing, delivery, and working capital.

Our understanding of stablecoins and blockchain technology pointed to a practical solution: combining round-the-clock settlement with local banking and payment networks. In 2020, we began building compliance-focused stablecoin financial infrastructure in Latin America, developing local operations, banking partnerships, liquidity management, and cross-border payment capabilities. We subsequently extended our reach to Asia and the United States. VelaFi was built around these business needs, helping companies collect, pay, and manage funds across borders more efficiently.
Explain the role of stablecoin in linking payment systems between Asia and Latin America.

Stablecoins provide a shared settlement layer that operates around the clock across different national payment systems. Trade between Asia and Latin America spans multiple currencies, time zones, and banking networks. Traditional payments can face delays from intermediary institutions, banking hours, and coordination between systems. Stablecoins can improve the cross-border settlement component, making money movement faster and more transparent.

For example, a Mexican importer paying an Asian supplier can fund a payment in pesos through a local bank. A provider handles the conversion, uses stablecoins for cross-border settlement, and delivers the agreed fiat currency through banking channels at the destination. Neither business necessarily needs to hold stablecoins or operate a digital wallet. This model is also discussed in Federal Reserve research on stablecoin cross-border payments.

Making this work requires reliable connections to local financial systems, including banking access, foreign-exchange liquidity, compliance, and collection and payout capabilities. Integrating these components can shorten the time funds spend in transit, improve payment predictability, and free up working capital.
Identify stablecoin growth trends in cross-border business-to-business (B2B) payments between companies in specific Latin American countries and Asian countries.

One clear trend is the growing use of stablecoins in supplier payments and routine corporate fund transfers. Along Mexico-China and Brazil-China trade corridors, Latin American importers need to pay Asian suppliers regularly, while Asian businesses need to collect sales proceeds from local markets. These activities require coordination between local-currency payments, foreign exchange, and cross-border settlement. Payments from Latin America to Chinese suppliers illustrate this demand.

Another growth area is corporate treasury activity connecting regional hubs such as Singapore and Hong Kong with Latin American markets. As businesses expand internationally, their needs extend beyond individual transfers to ongoing management of collections, supplier payments, and liquidity across countries. This creates demand for closer integration between stablecoin settlement, corporate financial systems, account management, and reconciliation.

Globally, McKinsey and Artemis research published in 2026 estimated annualized B2B stablecoin payments at approximately $226 billion, based on activity at the end of 2025 — roughly 60 percent of identified stablecoin payment volume. Established trade relationships and recurring treasury needs create substantial opportunities to expand these applications between Asia and Latin America.
What is VelaFi’s niche area in the global stablecoin market?

VelaFi specializes in payments and treasury infrastructure connecting businesses across Latin America, Asia, and the United States. We bring together local banking channels, stablecoin networks, foreign-exchange liquidity, and compliance workflows through a unified platform and APIs, supporting local collections and payouts, cross-border settlement, and multicurrency operations.

Our differentiation comes from deep market knowledge and years of local execution. Banking systems, regulatory requirements, and payment practices vary significantly across Latin America. Our local teams, banking and payment partnerships, compliance capabilities, and liquidity operations allow us to navigate that complexity. We also understand the needs of Asian businesses entering Latin America and can connect commercial and financial workflows across both regions.

We are incorporating AI into our next phase of product and operational development, focusing on payment routing, liquidity forecasting, automated reconciliation, and exception detection. Stablecoins improve how funds move and settle; AI can help businesses understand, plan, and manage those flows. Bringing these capabilities together with local financial networks is central to our development of a more intelligent global payments and treasury platform.
Assess the impact of U.S. stablecoin advancements on stablecoin markets in Asia and Latin America.

U.S. developments are creating a clearer institutional foundation for global enterprise adoption. The GENIUS Act and its ongoing implementation improve regulatory predictability, helping banks, payment providers, and businesses participate with greater confidence. A clearer framework also helps infrastructure companies like VelaFi serve enterprises and support adoption at greater scale.

As more financial institutions participate, capabilities in issuance, custody, liquidity, and banking connectivity can become more developed. This can create more options for payments between Asia and Latin America, improve cross-border settlement, and accelerate integration with existing financial systems.

The opportunity lies in connecting these global advances with local needs. Asia has extensive manufacturing, trade, and digital-services networks, while Latin American businesses need more efficient cross-border financial services. Combining stablecoin infrastructure with local banking access, payment networks, and compliance capabilities can bring those benefits to more companies. VelaFi’s operating experience and network across these regions position us to translate industry progress into practical payment and treasury capabilities that businesses can use every day.
